'''Iman Asante Shumpert''' (Born June 26, 1990) is sophomore at [[Georgia Tech]] and plays [[Point Guard]] for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball]] team.<ref name="cstv">{{cite web|url=http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/shumpert_iman00.html|title=Iman Shumpert|publisher=[[Georgia Tech Athletic Association]]|date=2010-03-29}}</ref>

==College career==
On 10/18/2007 he committed to play for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]].<ref>http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Iman-Shumpert-60898</ref>

During 2008-09 [[NCAA]] men's basketball season, he was GT's fourth-leading scorer for the season, both overall and in [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) games. In ACC games, he averaged 10.5 ppg, hitting 34.5 percent of his three-point attempts. He averaged 11.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and made 8-of-14 shots from the floor in two ACC Tournament games.<ref name="cstv"/>

He had 16 double-figure scoring games that season. He did go scoreless once at North Carolina (0-for-6 FG, 4 assists) on Feb. 28.<ref name="cstv"/>

He tied for first in the ACC in steals (2.1 pg) and had 22 in his last seven games, including a career-best six against Clemson on Feb. 22 and six in two ACC Tournament games.<ref name="cstv"/>

He scored a career-high 22 points Jan. 17 at NC State, and scored 18 points on two occasions (Vanderbilt, Virginia).<ref name="cstv"/>

At GT he is known as a gym rat with a high basketball IQ.<ref name="cstv"/>

==High school career==
He was first-team all-state player at [[Oak Park and River Forest High School]] and was one of the nation's top 30 seniors. He helped Oak Park and River Forest High School to three conference titles and was named conference MVP as a junior and senior.<ref name="cstv"/>

He was rated No. 15 among the nation's senior players by Scout.com and No. 26 by Rivals.com.<ref name="cstv"/>

==Personal==
Iman Shumpert's father Odis Shumpert is an insurance broker and his mother L'Tanya Shumpert is an adjunct professor of art and design at Columbia College in Chicago.<ref name="cstv"/>
